title: Streak Gauge — personal experiment log
content:
Purpose: quick day-to-day ledger for small inference tweaks I run locally / on dev pool. Keep it tiny, actionable, replayable. Notes-to-self style, not a formal report.

How I use this: run 3–6 short trials each day, capture p50/p90, tokens, cost estimate, and a one-line verdict. If something looks promising, move to a proper bench doc and tag RW-xxxx.

Mini table (columns: date | variant | bs | seq | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | tokens | est $/1k tok | notes/status)
2025-02-18 | av1-int8-kv | 8 | 512 | 32 | 78 | 2.1k | $0.12 | ok, weird spike at 45s in run3
2025-02-19 | av1-int8+cache | 8 | 512 | 28 | 62 | 2.0k | $0.10 | cache hit + prefix reused, stable
2025-02-20 | av1-fp16 | 8 | 512 | 26 | 59 | 2.2k | $0.14 | lower p90 but more cost; try smaller bs
2025-02-21 | av1-int8-kv | 4 | 1024 | 30 | 66 | 3.8k | $0.11 | batching changes p50 down, p90 similar
2025-02-24 | av1-int4-probe | 8 | 256 | 20 | 44 | 1.4k | $0.07 | quantization artifact in rare tokens — watch QA
2025-03-03 | av1-int4+kv | 8 | 256 | 19 | 41 | 1.3k | $0.06 | best perf/cost so far, small hallucination uptick

Quick takeaways (one-liners):
- int4 + KV cache consistently yields best cost/perf for short contexts (<=256).
- int8 still better for 512–1024 due to fewer QA regressions; p90 gap vs int4 narrows when active KV caching is enabled.
- Batch size trade: bs=8 wins for throughput tests, bs=4 reduces p90 for mixed latency-sensitive traces.

Hypotheses to validate next week:
- H1: Moving from int8 -> int4 with per-token quality filter will recover QA while keeping cost win. Quick test: int4 + simple rerank (top-3) for 200 examples.
- H2: Warm KV cache (prefix reuse >60%) reduces p90 by ~20% on avg for long-tail sequences; need synthetic reuse workload to simulate.

Action items (prioritized):
- [ ] Create a 200-example prompt set for the int4 + rerank check (owner: Sana) — target by 2025-03-07
- [ ] Script synthetic reuse driver for KV warmup (owner: Diego) — pair on 2025-03-05
- [ ] Push promising config to /dev pool and tag RW-2391 for allocation test (owner: Lila)

Notes-to-self / stray thoughts:
- Keep cheap metrics in this file only; canonical bench lives under shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/benchmarks when promoted.
- Remember to log seed and exact commit hash when promoting. Right now I just jot PR link in linked_artifacts.
- If hallucination rate >0.5% on regen, mark config as "needs-eval".

Unresolved/questions (quick):
- Why did 02/18 run spike on run3? Check infra logs for preemption or device clock scaling around 10:14 UTC. Jira-ish note: RW-2391 mentions intermittent cloud-driver throttling.
- Is cost estimator here (very rough $/1k tok) aligned with the dedicated pricing model? Probably not — double-check with finance before any customer-facing recommendation.

Micro checklist for promoting a config:
- perf: consistent p50/p90 across 5 runs
- cost: >10% better than baseline fp16 for target workload
- quality: no >1% regression on golden prompts
- infra: no device-side errors in logs

Recent small wins:
- 03/03 config (av1-int4+kv) reduced estimated token cost by 57% vs fp16 baseline for chat-like short prompts (<=256).

Reference commands (quick copy):
- run-local: ./run_trial.sh --model av1 --quant int4 --bs 8 --seq 256 --traces 100
- synthetic-warm: python tools/sim_kv_warm.py --pattern reuse-heavy --repeat 3

Slack refs / threads: see linked_artifacts for the thread where I dumped raw traces (thread: C12345).

"Notes to future-me": keep this daily for two weeks straight (streak metric), export to shared bench doc when a config survives both perf and quality checks.

End.
